lines.vo: Why can't you eat just a few chips?
That's not zero willpower. A lot of snack food is built to go down fast.
Kev tracks his snack attacks in his Break the Habit tracker.
In one NIH study, 20 adults lived in a lab for a month, two weeks on ultra-processed food and two weeks on less processed food.
On the ultra-processed menu, they ate about 500 more calories a day.
They also ate faster, which may leave your fullness signals less time to catch up.
So pour one portion into a bowl, and leave the bag in the kitchen.
One bowl, one check mark. That's how you stay on track.
